name: Brunner–Munzel relative-effect test
definition: Let h(x,y)=1(x<y)+0.5·1(x=y), p̂=Σ_iΣ_j h(X_i,Y_j)/(nm), A_i=Σ_j h(X_i,Y_j)/m, B_j=Σ_i h(X_i,Y_j)/n. W=(p̂−0.5)/√(s_A²/n+s_B²/m), with sample variances of A and B.
variables: X,Y independent groups; n,m≥2; p̂ relative-effect estimate; s_A²,s_B² unbiased sample variances; W studentized statistic
assumptions: Independent samples and independent observations within each group; nonzero estimated standard error; approximate reference distribution justified.
limitations: Small samples and zero variance may make the approximation unreliable; tests relative effect, not general equality of distributions.
failure_conditions: Zero estimated standard error or unmodelled dependence
computation: Compute tie-aware pairwise placements and their sample variances; obtain a justified t or asymptotic normal reference separately.

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, brunnermunzel API and references to Brunner and Munzel (2000). https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.brunnermunzel.html

application: Compare relative ordering between comparable independent measurements in development samples.
required_inputs: Two independent authorised samples of the same measurement with a prespecified relative-effect hypothesis.
incompatible_methods: Treating paired or clustered measurements as independent
mechanism_note: Studentizes a relative-effect estimate with separate group placement variances; unlike the equal-distribution Mann–Whitney null.

name: Bartlett homogeneity-of-variance test
definition: Let v_i=n_i−1, V=Σ_i v_i, s_p²=Σ_i v_i s_i²/V. B=[V ln(s_p²)−Σ_i v_i ln(s_i²)]/[1+(Σ_i 1/v_i−1/V)/(3(k−1))].
variables: k≥2 independent groups; n_i≥2 sizes; s_i² positive unbiased sample variances; B corrected likelihood-ratio statistic
assumptions: Independent normally distributed observations and groups; positive variances; chi-square approximation with k−1 degrees of freedom under equal variances.
limitations: Sensitive to non-normality; does not prove equality when non-significant.
failure_conditions: Zero group variance, severe non-normality or dependence
computation: Calculate pooled variance, log-variance contrast and finite-sample correction; use the approximate chi-square reference.

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, bartlett API and references. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bartlett.html

application: Assess variability across comparable independent groups when normality is defensible.
required_inputs: Authorised independent groups with sample sizes and positive unbiased variances.
incompatible_methods: Unadjusted use on correlated or heavily non-normal groups

name: Paired Student t-test
definition: For matched observations let d_i=x_i−y_i, T=mean(d)/(s_d/√n); under independent normally distributed differences with zero mean, T∼t_(n−1).
variables: n≥2 matched pairs; d_i difference; s_d positive unbiased sample standard deviation; T statistic
assumptions: Pairs correctly matched; differences independent across pairs and normally distributed for exact reference, or an adequate asymptotic approximation.
limitations: Serial or clustered differences require dependence-aware inference; extreme differences can dominate the mean.
failure_conditions: Zero difference variance, incorrect pairing or unmodelled serial dependence
computation: Form pairwise differences, calculate their sample mean and variance and evaluate the t reference with n−1 degrees of freedom.

application: Assess mean differences on matched development observations when pairwise independence is defensible.

incompatible_methods: Unmatched observations or ignoring time dependence
